body.x: NEWJAK Co., Ltd. (CEO Haehyun Jung) won a CES 2026 Innovation Award with its XR-based interactive sports content platform “SPORTRACK.”

NEWJAK has drawn global attention by presenting an education and sports convergence content strategy that combines immersive XR technology, allowing users to physically participate in real spaces without an HMD, with 16 physical education maps designed based on Korea’s 2023 revised national curriculum for elementary, middle, and high schools. The company received high evaluations for its structural practicality, which enables its application in actual physical education classes and sports training beyond conventional exhibition-style XR, as well as for its service model, which can expand into schools, public institutions, and the sports industry.

In this context, Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News and also a judge for the CES 2024 and CES 2026 Innovation Awards, met with NEWJAK CEO Haehyun Jung to discuss the background of the Innovation Award win, technological differentiation, scalability, and global market strategy.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: Please share your thoughts on winning the Innovation Award.

A. Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK: At first, I wondered, “Will this really work?” But once I tried it myself, I became confident that it could. The idea I pursued was in a field that did not yet exist in Korea, so many people told me, “Why don’t you make what consumers want?” Still, I pushed forward in the direction I believed in, and recent trends are proving that possibility. Receiving the Innovation Award in this context makes it even more meaningful.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: Please introduce NEWJAK.
A. Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK: The company name “NEWJAK” combines the English word “New” with the Chinese character “作 (jak),” meaning “to create,” conveying the idea of “creating new media.”

It originally came from the name of a course I taught as a part-time lecturer at a university. At the time, I ran a convergence class in which students from the New Media Content Department and the Composition Department collaborated to create performances, and I combined the first letters of each department to form the names “New” and “Jak.” Since the company originated from that class, our early business model focused on performance and event production until before the COVID-19 pandemic.

body.cap: Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News (left), and Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK (right), pose after the CES 2026 Innovation Company interview | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: What technology earned you the Innovation Award at CES 2025?

A. Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK: In the early days of the startup, I set the Arte Museum as a role model and tried to create similar media exhibitions. However, as I continued, I realized it was difficult for a small company to replicate that scale. In that process, our own unique content naturally emerged.

I then started thinking about “content that gives people a reason to come back repeatedly,” and I found the answer in e-sports. Seeing my nephew receive prize money as a professional gamer made me realize the market potential, and I developed it into “interactive content that people physically participate in,” combined with immersive media spaces. This technology was recognized as a CES 2025 Innovation Award honoree.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: Please introduce the technology that won the CES 2026 Innovation Award.

A. Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK: At CES 2025, we won an Innovation Award with XR content based on digital jump rope. After showcasing it, we received far more inquiries than expected from sports organizations, including the Korea Sports Promotion Foundation, which clearly confirmed that this technology could expand into education and sports.

As a result, at CES 2026, we positioned sports more explicitly. Based on the 2023 revised national curriculum for elementary, middle, and high schools, we developed 16 XR physical education maps in the form of a board game. We plan to complete all content this year and aim for actual school adoption next year.

Unlike most existing XR approaches that require wearing an HMD, our solution allows multiple people to participate together without equipment. The most prominent feature is that physical education classes can take place immediately in an empty classroom measuring 6 meters by 6 meters.

body.cap: NEWJAK, winner of the Innovation Award in the XR & Spatial Computing category | Source: CES

body.x: Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: What are your plans for CES 2026 participation?

A. Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK: When I first attended CES, my expectations were high, to the point of dreaming of the “American Dream.” But once there, I also saw the reality that small companies struggle to stand out among the flashy booths of large corporations. However, after participating consistently, I became convinced that meeting even one right partner can lead to meaningful results. This year, we discussed an MOU and NDA with one company at CES, and we are also debating IP sharing and joint development with a well-known Japanese company.

At CES 2026, a hands-on experience zone will be set up in the joint pavilion so visitors can try a mini version of the demo. While our Korean showroom uses all six surfaces to create an immersive XR space, CES regulations impose limitations, so this time we will configure only four surfaces: front, left, right, and floor. Even so, we plan to deliver the highest level of immersion possible.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: What achievements did you make this year, and what are your plans?

A. Haehyun Jung, CEO of NEWJAK: SPORTRACK, was selected for the Korea Creative Content Agency’s Functional Game Production Project, through which we completed all 16 physical education contents. While the funding itself was not significant, having a clear deadline throughout the project period allowed us to complete our own content without being pushed aside by outsourced work. For a small company, such deadlines serve as a strong driving force to continue development.

Another significant achievement this year was being selected for the XR system construction project at the Korea Army Training Center. Installation is currently underway, and from January next year, all young men entering the Nonsan Training Center will experience the XR content we created. We expect this to become one of the first cases of XR being fully utilized in the public sector.
From now on, we plan to expand into various sports such as golf and baseball within six-surface XR spaces to deliver even higher levels of immersion. We see enormous scalability in sports content.
